source_metadata.exact_title: Ibrutinib, obinutuzumab, and venetoclax in relapsed and untreated patients with mantle cell lymphoma: a phase 1/2 trial

batch_manifest.scope: supplement S3-S4 regimen and TLS prevention
dose finding and main safety results/Table 2

consistency_findings.finding: The main Results section reports cohort B 1-year PFS 74.5% and OS 87.5%; the abstract separately reports 2-year PFS 69.5% and OS 68.6%. These are different time horizons, not treated as a contradiction.

MRD percentages differ depending on denominator: Table 3 reports intent-to-treat-like cohort percentages (e.g., cohort B 10/24 = 42%), while narrative molecular-response rates use only MRD-evaluable patients (10/14 = 71.4%). Atoms preserve the evaluable denominator when reporting molecular response.
Cohort A lacks venetoclax and is not a randomized comparator; cross-cohort efficacy or toxicity differences cannot establish the incremental effect of venetoclax.

extraction_limitations: The 62-page supplement contains exhaustive adverse-event tables (S8/S9). This extraction atomizes the main article safety table, dose-finding safety, TLS events, and selected supplement compliance/amendment data, but does not create a separate atom for every low-grade or rare supplemental AE row.
Cheson and Lugano criteria reproduced as images/tables in supplement S5-S6 were treated as referenced assessment frameworks rather than re-atomized criterion-by-criterion.
The supplement amendment table is dense and historically layered; only amendments that materially affect venetoclax dosing, TLS mitigation, and cohort C were atomized.
No unreported study detail was inferred. Calculated percentages are explicitly labeled calculated_from_reported_data or tagged calculated_percentage.
schema_gaps: The current LiteratureAtom schema has no dedicated protocol-amendment kind; material amendments are represented as method atoms with descriptive tags.
The schema has no dedicated treatment-adherence/compliance kind; drug-administration percentages are represented as quantitative_result atoms.
QuantitativeResult supports one principal estimate per atom; multi-timepoint or multi-cohort results are therefore split into separate atoms.
